label: conj:proton-borromean-assembly
title: The proton's Borromean mass assembly: multiplicity $\dim V_{(2,1)} = 2$ and binding count $|S_3| = 6$
html:
Conjecture. The proton's Borromean mass assembly: multiplicity \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2 and binding count |S_3| = 6

Conjecture (proton Borromean mass assembly). The proton mass assembles from the Borromean categorical observable F_{\mathrm{Bor}} (def:f-bor-borromean-observable) according to

  m_p \;=\; \mathrm{mult} \cdot \bigl(m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) \;-\; \mathrm{bind} \cdot m_e\bigr),

where the two structural integers are the categorical invariants of H_3(q):

  • the constituent multiplicity \mathrm{mult} = \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2, the dimension of the trace-dominant Hecke irrep, and
  • the per-constituent electron-binding count \mathrm{bind} = |S_3| = 6 (so 12 = \mathrm{mult}\cdot\mathrm{bind} = 2\cdot 6 = |S_3|\cdot\dim V_{(2,1)}).

Established identifications and the residual bridge

The numerical identity m_p = 2\,m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) - 12\,m_e is verified to 0.24\,\mathrm{ppm} at 50-dps MPFR, and each factor has an established categorical identification:

  • F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, q)| \cdot [3]_q!/q^3 is the Borromean Markov-trace observable (categorical, def:f-bor-borromean-observable);
  • the transpose-pair identity y_{(3)}(q)\cdot y_{(1,1,1)}(q) = 1/[3]_q!^2 is Lean-proved;
  • the integer 12 = 2\cdot 6 = \mathrm{mult}\cdot\mathrm{bind} is a categorical count (|S_3|\cdot\dim V_{(2,1)}), and not the inverse of an Ocneanu leading-pole coefficient -\tfrac{1}{12}: the Markov trace of \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} has a q^{-4} pole of coefficient 1, not the q^{-10}\cdot(-\tfrac{1}{12}) of the measured no-interface braid. That identification is refuted for \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} and is not part of the derivation.

What remains conjectural is the bridge from these identifications to the assembly law above — specifically why the trace-dominant irrep's dimension \dim V_{(2,1)} enters as a linear multiplier and |S_3| as the electron-binding count. The Wedderburn block expansion of the Markov trace (the (2,1) block carries \approx 49\% of the proton's T_1 contribution) is the natural framework, but the formal categorical statement is pending.

The conjecture is axiomatised as the Lean class QOU.AppendixQValues.ProtonBorromeanAssembly: its fields are exactly these hypotheses (the two structural integers and the factored assembly law), and prop:proton-mass-substrate-identity derives the published flat identity from them, sorry-free modulo the class instance.
